title: Exploration via Exploitation: The Blessing of Reward Diversity in Personalized Federated RL
claim: Two distinct kinds of reward heterogeneity each keep the cross-agent average visitation balanced, whatever the assumed transition kernel.
layout: 2 stacked rows, left-to-right: MDP diagram, rewards, Q-gap plot with bars
description: The figure has two horizontal rows, Regime I on top and Regime II below, separated by a dashed line. Each row has the same layout. On the left is a small two-step MDP: a circle X with arrows labeled up and down to circles Y1 and Y2. Red text gives agent A's rewards and blue text gives agent B's. In Regime I the rewards depend on the action. In Regime II they depend on the state. In the middle, an equation shows the matching step-2 values. On the right is a plot of the Q-gap against the kernel P1, with a solid red line for agent A and a dashed blue line for agent B. Regime I has flat lines at +1 and -1. Regime II has crossing, mirrored lines. Small red and blue-hatched bar charts for up and down visitations sit at both ends of each plot. A legend runs along the bottom.
caption: Two regimes of reward heterogeneity that induce global coverage in Assumption [ref], illustrated on a common two-step MDP with $\mathcal{S} = \{x, Y_1, Y_2\}$, $\mathcal{A} = \{\textup{up}, \textup{down}\}$, $M = 2$ (agent A and agent B). In each row, the right panel plots each agent's step-1 Q-gap $\tilde{Q}^m_{gap} = \tilde{Q}_1^m(x, \textup{up}) - \tilde{Q}_1^m(x, \textup{down})$, whose sign determines the agent's greedy choice at $x$, as the assumed kernel $\tilde{P}_1$ varies. Top (Regime I): action-dependent state-independent rewards make $\tilde{V}_2^m$ take the same value at every state, so each agent's Q-gap is fixed regardless of $\tilde{P}_1$ (horizontal lines). Both agents persistently select different actions, and the cross-agent average visitation remains $1/2$ on each action at both extremes of $\tilde{P}_1$. Bottom (Regime II): state-dependent action-independent rewards anti-correlated across agents make $\tilde{V}_2^A + \tilde{V}_2^B$ take the same value at every state, so the two agents' Q-gaps are exact mirror images for any $\tilde{P}_1$ (crossing lines). Individual visitations swap between the two extremes (blue and red bars exchange positions), but the cross-agent average remains $1/2$ on each action throughout.
abstract: While federated reinforcement learning (RL) has traditionally guaranteed high efficiency in homogeneous environments, collaboration is often hindered when agents possess distinct goals. In this paper, we flip this paradigm, framing reward heterogeneity not as a hurdle to consensus, but as a structural asset that catalyzes exploration. We first propose Personalized Federated Upper Confidence Bound Value Iteration (PF-UCBVI), which achieves optimal linear speedup by decoupling shared dynamics from personalized objectives. To eliminate the risks of explicit exploration, we then introduce Personalized Federated Exploration-Free Value Iteration (PF-EFVI), a purely greedy algorithm that leverages reward diversity to ensure state-action coverage. We prove that PF-EFVI attains logarithmic regret without explicit exploration bonuses under sufficient reward diversity. Our results reveal that agent disagreement shifts the exploration burden from temporal complexity to spatial diversity, enabling efficient collective learning without explicit exploration.
